citation: Bakker, F.C., de Ruiter, J.W.E., van der Hout, A., van Koningsveld, M. (2026) Accurately forecasting saltwater intrusion through navigation locks requires nautical traffic simulation modelling. Ocean Engineering. doi:10.1016/j.oceaneng.2026.124918

dedupe_keys.name: coupled sea lock formulation and opentnsim model of saltwater intrusion through navigation locks

description: This model couples an analytical lock exchange model, the Sea Lock Formulation, with the nautical traffic simulator OpenTNSim to forecast how much salt water enters inland waters through navigation locks. It was published in Ocean Engineering in 2026 by Floor Bakker, Jikke de Ruiter, Arne van der Hout and Mark van Koningsveld of Delft University of Technology and Deltares. Analytical lock exchange models are efficient but depend on scarce records of gate status; during droughts, strategies that limit salt intrusion delay vessels, so both effects must be weighed. The coupled method derives time-varying lock operation parameters from accessible vessel data and evaluates mitigation strategies for salt intrusion and traffic performance together. Applied to the IJmuiden sea lock, the largest lock in the world, and validated against measured salt concentrations and operation records, it reduced long-term salt intrusion errors in forecasting from +22.2 percent to -2.6 percent without calibration. Coverage: one lock; the method is transferable to other sea locks. Access: open-access article; whether the coupling code is released was not confirmed. Licence and cost: the article is CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: one validation site and a hybrid analytical approach, not full hydrodynamics. It supports climate adaptation and capacity planning of locks under drought. It extends the OpenTNSim model and complements the SIVAK lock simulation in the catalogue.
